drivingQuestion: How can the mishna impose a fine on one who violates his sister when the Makkot mishna says he is flogged?
outcomeNote: the contradiction is raised here; its resolution falls in the following unit

segments.he: הַבָּא עַל אֲחוֹתוֹ וְעַל אֲחוֹת אָבִיו כּוּ׳. וּרְמִינְהוּ, אֵלּוּ הֵן הַלּוֹקִין: הַבָּא עַל אֲחוֹתוֹ, וְעַל אֲחוֹת אָבִיו, וְעַל אֲחוֹת אִמּוֹ, וְעַל אֲחוֹת אִשְׁתּוֹ, וְעַל אֵשֶׁת אָחִיו, וְעַל אֵשֶׁת אֲחִי אָבִיו, וְעַל הַנִּדָּה.
segments.en: § The mishna continues: Similarly, «one who has» forced «relations with his sister,» i.e., he rapes her, «or with his father’s sister,» or with his mother’s sister, or with his wife’s sister, or with his brother’s wife, or with his father’s brother’s wife after they divorced, or with a menstruating woman, there is a fine paid. «And» the Gemara «raised a contradiction» from the following mishna (Makkot 13a): «And these» people «are flogged: One who has relations with his sister, or with his father’s sister, or with his mother’s sister, or with his wife’s sister, or with his brother’s wife, or with his father’s brother’s wife, or with a menstruating woman.» Anyone who intentionally has relations with any of these women is punished with lashes.
